content: Colchicine is prescribed to alleviate swelling and pain associated with gout or gouty arthritis attacks. It can also be taken regularly to prevent such attacks. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Colchicine is available as an oral tablet. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take colchicine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using colchicine to relieve symptoms of a gout attack, begin taking it at the first sign of pain. Relief typically begins within 12 hours, and symptoms usually resolve within 48 to 72 hours. The medication will not be as effective if you delay taking it after the onset of pain. Before taking colchicine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to colchicine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially vitamin B12 and other vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had stomach, intestinal, blood disorders, or kidney, liver, or heart problems. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking colchicine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for a urine test, inform your doctor and laboratory personnel that you are taking colchicine, as it may affect test results. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Colchicine may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, severe rash, difficulty breathing, seizures, unusual bleeding or bruising, or blood in the urine or stool. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store colchicine in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to colchicine. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
